product.name: Tasky
product.summary: A small personal task manager that keeps everything in your browser
product.description: Tasky is the Orbit reference application: a deliberately small, real task manager with lists, due dates, Today and Overdue views, and local-only storage.

entities.name: Task Management
entities.summary: Create, maintain, finish and remove personal tasks
entities.description: Everything a person does to keep their own to-do items up to date: capturing a task, changing its details, ticking it off and deleting it when it no longer matters.

entities.name: Create and Edit Tasks
entities.summary: Capture a task and change its title, notes, due date or list
entities.description: A task needs a title; notes, a due date and the list it belongs to are optional. People can come back later and change any of those details in an accessible dialog without losing their place in the list.

behaviors.name: Create a task
behaviors.expected: A task with a non-blank title can be created with optional notes and due date, and it appears in the list the person is viewing straight away.

behaviors.name: Reject blank titles
behaviors.expected: Submitting an empty or whitespace-only title keeps the dialog open, explains that a title is required next to the field, and saves nothing.

behaviors.name: Edit task details
behaviors.expected: Title, notes, due date and list of an existing task can be changed in one dialog, and the changes are visible in the list immediately and when the task is reopened.

behaviors.name: Accessible task dialog
behaviors.expected: The task dialog moves keyboard focus into itself, keeps Tab and Shift+Tab inside it, closes on Escape, and returns focus to the control that opened it.

entities.name: Complete and Delete Tasks
entities.summary: Tick tasks off, reopen them, or delete them for good
entities.description: Finishing a task is a single action that can be undone; deleting is permanent, so it always asks first. Every control has a spoken label that names the task.

behaviors.name: Complete and reopen a task
behaviors.expected: Marking a task complete removes it from the default list view (it stays reachable with "Show completed"), and marking it incomplete again restores it.

behaviors.name: Delete only after confirmation
behaviors.expected: Choosing delete opens a confirmation naming the task; cancelling leaves the task untouched and only confirming removes it permanently.

behaviors.name: Labeled, keyboard-operable task controls
behaviors.expected: Each task exposes controls named after it ("Mark 'Buy milk' complete", "Delete 'Buy milk'") that work with the keyboard alone.

entities.name: Task Organization
entities.summary: Group tasks into lists and decide which list each task lives in
entities.description: Tasks always belong to exactly one list: the built-in Inbox or a custom list the person created.

entities.name: Custom Lists
entities.summary: Create, rename and delete personal lists; Inbox is always there
entities.description: People can group related tasks into lists such as Work or Errands. Inbox is built in and cannot be renamed or deleted. Deleting a list never deletes its tasks.

behaviors.name: Create and rename lists
behaviors.expected: A new list can be created and an existing list renamed from the list view; the sidebar and heading update immediately and the list keeps its tasks.

behaviors.name: Reject blank and duplicate list names
behaviors.expected: A list name must contain visible text and must differ (ignoring case) from every other list name and from "Inbox"; otherwise an inline message explains why and nothing is saved.

behaviors.name: Inbox cannot be renamed or deleted
behaviors.expected: The Inbox view offers no rename or delete action, and attempts to rename or delete Inbox programmatically are refused.

behaviors.name: Deleting a list moves its tasks to Inbox
behaviors.expected: Before a list is deleted the confirmation states how many tasks will move to Inbox; after confirming, every task of that list (completed ones included) is in Inbox and none are lost.

entities.name: Task Assignment
entities.summary: Decide which list a task belongs to, by default and later
entities.description: A new task lands in Inbox unless it is created while viewing a custom list. A task can be moved to another list at any time by editing it.

behaviors.name: New tasks default to Inbox
behaviors.expected: A task created from Inbox, Today or All Tasks is placed in Inbox, while a task created inside a custom list view is placed in that list.

behaviors.name: Move a task between lists
behaviors.expected: Changing the list of a task in the edit dialog removes it from its old list view and shows it in the new one.

entities.name: Task Discovery
entities.summary: Find the right tasks through Inbox, Today, All Tasks and lists
entities.description: Views that answer "what is in this list?", "what needs attention today?" and "what do I have in total?".

behaviors.name: Navigation stays reachable on narrow screens
behaviors.expected: Below 720px wide the sidebar collapses behind a Menu button that opens and closes it, and every view and list remains reachable.

entities.name: Inbox and All Tasks
entities.summary: See what is in Inbox, a list, or everything at once
entities.description: Inbox and each custom list show only their own tasks and hide finished ones unless asked. All Tasks shows every task, with finished tasks after open ones, and each view has a helpful empty state.

behaviors.name: Inbox shows only Inbox tasks
behaviors.expected: The Inbox view lists only tasks in Inbox, hides completed tasks until "Show completed" is switched on, and its sidebar count equals the number of open Inbox tasks.

behaviors.name: All Tasks includes completed tasks last
behaviors.expected: All Tasks lists every task from every list, open tasks first ordered by due date (undated last) and completed tasks after them.

behaviors.name: Helpful empty states
behaviors.expected: An empty Inbox, Today, All Tasks or custom list each says in plain words why it is empty and what to do next.

entities.name: Today and Overdue
entities.summary: See everything due today or already late, across all lists
entities.description: Today gathers incomplete tasks due today or earlier from every list. Late tasks are clearly marked in words, and the view stays correct when the day changes.

behaviors.name: Today lists tasks due today or earlier
behaviors.expected: Today shows incomplete tasks whose due date is today or earlier from every list; tasks due later, without a due date, or already completed are not shown.

behaviors.name: Overdue tasks are labeled in words
behaviors.expected: A task whose due date is before today shows the word "Overdue" next to its due date, so lateness never depends on color alone.

behaviors.name: Today follows the local calendar day
behaviors.expected: When the local date changes (at midnight, or when the window or tab is revisited) Today re-evaluates: yesterday's due tasks become Overdue and tasks due on the new day appear without reloading.

behaviors.name: Today follows a changed time zone
behaviors.expected: After the device time zone changes, Today and Overdue are computed against the new local date as soon as the window regains focus.

entities.name: Local Data
entities.summary: Everything Tasky stores, kept in this browser only
entities.description: One versioned document in browser localStorage holds lists and tasks. Nothing leaves the device and there are no accounts. The repositories below share this storage helper.

behaviors.name: Unreadable data is never overwritten
behaviors.expected: If the stored document is not valid JSON or fails validation, Tasky shows a banner offering "Download raw data" and "Start fresh", does not crash, and writes nothing until the person chooses.

behaviors.name: Starting fresh keeps a backup
behaviors.expected: Choosing "Start fresh" copies the unreadable raw text to a separate backup storage key before clearing the main key.

behaviors.name: Demo data only on request
behaviors.expected: Sample lists and tasks are written only after explicit "Load demo data" or confirmed "Reset demo data"; existing data is never reseeded, even when it is empty.

behaviors.name: Failed saves are reported
behaviors.expected: When the browser refuses a write (for example storage is full or blocked) the person sees an error message and the previously saved data is left intact.

entities.name: Task Repository
entities.description: Validates and persists task changes (create, update, complete, delete) in the shared local document and stamps createdAt/updatedAt.

behaviors.name: Creating a task normalizes it
behaviors.expected: A created task gets a unique id, a trimmed title, Inbox as list unless one is given, completed=false and equal createdAt/updatedAt timestamps.

behaviors.name: Invalid input is rejected without writing
behaviors.expected: Blank titles, impossible calendar dates and unknown list ids raise a validation error and leave storage unchanged.

behaviors.name: Updates keep identity and refresh updatedAt
behaviors.expected: Updating or completing a task keeps its id and createdAt, advances updatedAt, and deleting removes only that task.

behaviors.name: Changes survive reload
behaviors.expected: Task changes are written to the versioned storage key immediately, so a new repository over the same storage (or a page reload) sees the same tasks.

entities.name: List Repository
entities.summary: Reads and writes custom list records
entities.description: Creates, renames and deletes custom lists; Inbox is virtual and never stored. Deleting a list rewrites its tasks to Inbox in the same write.

behaviors.name: List names are unique and non-blank
behaviors.expected: Creating or renaming a list with a blank name, a case-insensitive duplicate or the name "Inbox" is rejected; a valid rename keeps the list id.

behaviors.name: List deletion is atomic and lossless
behaviors.expected: Deleting a list removes it and reassigns each of its tasks to Inbox in a single write, reports how many tasks moved, and never deletes tasks.

entities.name: Presentation Logic
entities.summary: Pure rules that decide what the screens show
entities.description: Framework-free functions that turn stored data and the current local date into the ordered task lists and badges that the interface renders.

entities.name: Task Filtering and Sorting
entities.summary: Selects and orders tasks for each view
entities.description: Implements which tasks belong to Inbox, a custom list, Today and All Tasks, whether completed tasks are shown, and the one deterministic ordering used everywhere.

behaviors.name: Deterministic task ordering
behaviors.expected: Tasks are ordered incomplete first, then by due date ascending with undated tasks last, then by createdAt, then by id, independent of storage order.

behaviors.name: Today selection rule
behaviors.expected: The Today filter returns exactly the incomplete tasks with a due date on or before the supplied local date, from every list, in standard order.

behaviors.name: Completed tasks are hidden except where requested
behaviors.expected: Every view hides completed tasks unless showCompleted is set, except All Tasks, which always includes them after open tasks; sidebar counts include only open tasks.

entities.name: Local Date Evaluation
entities.summary: Works out today, overdue and day rollover from the local calendar
entities.description: Converts an injectable "now" into the user's local calendar date and answers whether a due date is today, overdue, or due later; also schedules re-evaluation at the next local midnight.

behaviors.name: Local calendar date, not UTC
behaviors.expected: The current date is read from the local year, month and day of the supplied instant, so late-evening and early-morning times map to the date shown on the wall clock.

behaviors.name: Overdue and due-today classification
behaviors.expected: A due date before the local date is overdue, a due date on or before it counts for Today, and a missing due date is neither.

behaviors.name: Day rollover re-evaluation
behaviors.expected: The delay to the next local midnight is computed exactly, and a due-today task is classified overdue once the local date advances.

relationships.description: Creating and editing tasks is carried out by TaskRepository.create and TaskRepository.update, which validate and persist the change.
Completing and deleting tasks call TaskRepository.setCompleted and TaskRepository.remove.
List creation, renaming and deletion (including moving tasks to Inbox) are performed by ListRepository.
A task's list is stored on the task record and validated by TaskRepository on create and update.
The Today view is the "today" filter in filtering.ts, ordered by the shared comparator.
Today can only show tasks that exist and carry the due dates entered through create and edit.
Assigning a task to a list requires lists to exist and be managed by Custom Lists.
What Inbox contains is decided by assignment: the Inbox default and tasks moved there from deleted lists.
The Today view and the Overdue label use the local date and the midnight rollover timer from Local Date Evaluation.
filterTasks calls isDueTodayOrOverdue to decide Today membership.
Inbox, custom list and All Tasks views are produced by filterTasks and sorted by compareTasks.
